question.text: Item (g) of the SEBI-prescribed Code of Conduct for Managers of AIF and their key management personnel requires the manager to:

answer.text: Record in writing the investment, divestment and other key decisions, together with appropriate justification for such decisions
Provide investors with daily NAV reports via SMS
Publish all portfolio company names on the AIF's public website
Submit monthly scorecards to the AMFI code of ethics committee

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.10 (Code of Conduct), item (g) explicitly requires the Manager to 'Record in writing, the investment, divestment and other key decisions, together with appropriate justification for such decisions.' This creates the IC-minutes audit trail. The Trap: Daily SMS NAV is not AIF practice. Public portfolio-name disclosure would breach investee confidentiality (Code item (n)). AMFI scorecards apply to mutual funds, not AIFs. Cross-Exam Context: Similar record-keeping duty tested in X-A/X-B (Investment Advisers) and XV (Research Analyst), but with different record horizons. Manager's Pro-Tip: IC minutes should record dissenting votes and the reasons. 'Approved unanimously' entries hide governance weakness — SEBI inspections flag ICs with 100% unanimous approvals.
